about: Common glossary of the user interface texts. Every Str.* text of the other languages that translates an English text containing a term below must contain one of the accepted forms of that term (test GlossaryTests). docs/GLOSSARY.md is generated from this file; to regenerate it run the tests with FSS_WRITE_GLOSSARY=1.
matching: Texts are compared in lower case. Placeholders such as {0}, file names (scripts.lst, parser.dll, .ssl), underscores (access keys) and the phrases of "ignore" are removed first.

English: a term applies to a key when one of its "en" variants occurs as a whole word (case-insensitive) in the English text; text between single or double quotes without a blank (such as 'Node') is skipped.

Other languages: the text must contain one of the "accept" fragments (plain substrings, so that inflected forms and German compounds match). A fragment that starts with ^ must start at a word start, one that ends with $ must end a word.
"forbid" fragments (same syntax) must not occur in a text where the term applies. "forbiddenEverywhere" fragments must not occur in any text of the language.
"enForbid": English wordings that must not be used (the English texts are checked too).

terms.notes: An SSL source file (.ssl) or its compiled form (.int). Keep the English loan word where the language already does ("script" in es/fr/it/pt); never "program" or "file" alone.
An SSL procedure (the unit of code; a dialogue node is a procedure). Never "function" (that is a built-in/engine function) and never "subroutine".
An engine/sfall function or a user code snippet of the function tree. Not the same as a procedure.
A script, local, argument or global variable.
A #define macro of the preprocessor.
A #define (preprocessor definition) or "where something is defined" (Go to definition). Not "declaration".
Where a procedure or variable is declared (Go to declaration).
A header file (*.h) with macros, procedures and variables shared between scripts. Spell the file kind out: "header file". Do not use "include" for the file itself.
The #include directive and the file it pulls in. The keyword #include itself is never translated.
A numbered text of a .msg message file (NPC line, player reply, UI message of the game). "Message file" = the .msg file; say "message file", never ".msg file" or "messages file".
The conversation between the player and an NPC. (A "dialog" in the sense of a window is a dialog box, not this term.)
A node of the dialogue flowchart = an NPC/player dialogue procedure (Node001...). Always "node", not "block", "box" or "step".
The dialogue flowchart window/file (.fcd). A short form ("diagram" in es/it/cs, "schemat" in pl) is accepted when the context is clear.
The player character (PC) that answers in a dialogue. Gender-neutral wherever the language allows.
An engine/sfall opcode. The word stays "opcode" (not translated) in every language.
Adding a script to scripts.lst (register). Not the Windows registry and not "save".
A script template (.ssl) or a node code template.
The Fallout game archive (master.dat / critter.dat). es/pt use the same word as for "file" (archivo/arquivo); zh: 档案, never 存档 (that means a saved game).
A piece of code the editor inserts from a trigger word or a list (Insert Snippet, Surround With), with tab stops. Not the same as a template (a whole script or a node).
Turning an .ssl script into an .int (the compile verb and its nouns).
The compiler program (sslc, compile.exe).
Turning an .int back into .ssl (int2ssl or the built-in decompiler).
Running the C-style preprocessor (mcpp/wcc/built-in) before the compiler.
Compile a script and decompile it back to check the result. Written "Round trip" in English.
The script parser that supplies procedures, variables and errors. es/fr/pt translate it (analizador, analyseur, analisador); the other languages keep "parser" (ru: парсер, zh: 解析器).
The native parser (parser.dll, x86) as opposed to the built-in C# parser. zh: 原生, not 本机.
Shipped inside the editor (built-in parser/decompiler). Not "internal" and not "native".
A program outside the editor (external editor, external decompiler).
A project folder with an optional fss-project.json.
An entry of the Errors tab / problem list (error, warning or information).
The Settings window and the settings file (Visual Studio: Options/Settings). "Options" is reserved for a menu of toggles.
The light/dark colour theme (Windows/Visual Studio wording).
The UI or message language.
The script editor, the message editor, an external editor.
A directory on disk. Never "directory" or "path" for the folder itself.
The text encoding / code page used to read and write files.
The log panel / build log / parser log / log file (Windows wording "registro", "journal", "Protokoll").
Find references: the places that use a symbol.
Rename a symbol, node, file or macro.
Message file <-> script association, and the Windows file type association.
Fold an outline region (procedure) of the editor or a node of the flowchart.
Unfold an outline region.
Comment / uncomment code; a comment line of a .msg file.
Left indentation of code.
The text cursor of the editor (not the mouse pointer).
Find / Search (text, references, files). Same verb family for both in most languages (Visual Studio: Find/Search).
Replace text.
The case-sensitive search option.
The whole-word search option.
The regular-expression search option.
Read a file again from disk (discarding unsaved changes). Not "refresh" and not "update".
Changes that were not written to disk yet.
Write to disk. fr: enregistrer (also reserved for Save; "register" uses inscrire).
Cancel an operation or a dialog.
Permanently delete data (procedure, node, file, line). "Remove" is for taking an entry out of a list.
Take an entry out of a list or strip characters (not a destructive delete).
Undo the last edit.
Redo the undone edit.
A compiler/parser warning (below an error).
A compiler/parser/tool error.
